title: Closing snapshot can ingest a newly introduced Tier-A secret
confidence: high (0.96) for the interleaving trace; medium for occurrence frequency
summary: Manual snapshot and index build a preview-time exclusion set from currently ignored Tier-A names, but the closing snapshot re-enumerates the scope and only applies that stale set before raw persistence. A lower-trust local or synced writer who introduces a new `.env`, PEM, or other Tier-A direct child after preview can cause KCS to write the plaintext raw object and publish it in local commit history.

codeEvidence.label: Manual snapshot derives exclusions from preview-time ignored names
codeEvidence.explanation: The manual snapshot entrypoint classifies only the direct children present during `build_scan_preview()` and sends the resulting ignored names to the snapshot path as a `BTreeSet` of strings.

codeEvidence.label: Index uses the same preview-to-exclusion pattern before auto snapshot
codeEvidence.explanation: `index` also turns the preview candidates into a stale exclusion set. The later auto snapshot receives only names that were ignored at preview time, not a classifier or bound candidate identity.

codeEvidence.label: Closing enumeration checks only the stale path set
codeEvidence.explanation: The core snapshot path independently re-enumerates the root. A newly introduced Tier-A name is accepted unless its exact name already appears in the preview-derived `excluded_paths` set.

codeEvidence.label: Unexcluded current file bytes are written as raw objects
codeEvidence.explanation: Once the new file name misses the stale exclusion set, `store_raw` snapshot mode persists the plaintext bytes and publishes a tree entry under that name.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that Tier-A classification must apply to the file that is actually persisted. The CLI classifies a preview of the directory, but `Repository::build_working_tree_with_normalize()` performs the authoritative enumeration later and checks only a stale set of preview names before reading and writing raw bytes.

validation.method: static source trace plus local/offline synthetic PoC
validation.summary: The source trace confirms two separate enumerations: preview-time classification produces ignored names, while closing snapshot performs a path-only rescan that does not rerun Tier-A classification. The PoC models the same interleaving with temporary synthetic files.
assertions: Tier-A files present during preview are correctly excluded.
A new Tier-A file introduced after preview is absent from `excluded_paths`.
`build_working_tree_with_normalize()` has no secret classifier before `fs::read()` and `write_raw()`.
limitations: No barrier-controlled live KCS race was executed.
Race timing frequency was not measured.
The PoC uses synthetic temporary files and does not read real secrets or touch a real KCS store.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust local or synced contributor introduces `.env`, a PEM file, or another Tier-A direct child during the preview-to-snapshot interval. The closing snapshot sees the new file, misses it in the stale exclusion set, and archives the plaintext into local CAS and commit history.

dataflow.summary: preview candidates -> ignored-name set -> delayed `build_working_tree_with_normalize()` enumeration -> `excluded_paths.contains()` miss -> `fs::read()` -> `write_raw()` -> tree entry
dataflow.source: concurrent direct-child create or rename by a lower-trust local/synced contributor
dataflow.sink: plaintext raw object and commit-history reference in the owner-only local KCS store
dataflow.outcome: newly introduced Tier-A content crosses the secret-exclusion boundary into archive history

reachability.summary: The attacker needs write or rename authority in the selected scope and must land the new Tier-A name between preview and closing enumeration during a manual snapshot or index operation.
reachability.attacker: lower-trust local or synced content contributor
reachability.entrypoint: manual `snapshot` or non-preview `index` covering the mutable scope
preconditions: Concurrent write or rename access to the selected scope.
A Tier-A direct-child file introduced after preview.
The new file is readable by the KCS process.
The operator completes a snapshot or index operation covering that interval.
reachability.outcome: one newly introduced Tier-A direct child can be archived per successful interleaving

impact.why: Secret-classified local content can be unintentionally retained in plaintext raw CAS and commit history, though immediate disclosure outside the owner-only archive was not shown.

likelihood.why: Concurrent mutation by a local or synced contributor is plausible, but practical timing was not measured and the workflow is operator mediated.

limitations: Stable secrets present during preview are excluded correctly.
No automatic remote send follows directly from this archived object.
The owner-only `.kcs` store limits immediate exposure.

remediation.summary: Reclassify every closing-snapshot entry before raw persistence, or bind preview candidates to an expected name and byte identity and reject drift before publication.
regressionTests: Manual snapshot: create `.env` after preview and before closing enumeration; assert it is not persisted.
`index` auto snapshot: create a PEM file after the pipeline preview and before auto snapshot; assert it is excluded.
Control: a Tier-A file present during preview remains excluded.
Control: ordinary benign files still snapshot as intended under the chosen identity-binding policy.
